en: In the moral world-view we see consciousness itself producing its object with consciousness; we see it neither finding that same object as something alien, nor yet becoming unconscious of it, but rather proceeding everywhere according to a ground from which it posits the objective essence; it thus knows that same as itself, for it knows itself as the one that acts and produces it.
It thus seems to come to rest and satisfaction here, for it can find this only where it no longer needs to go beyond its object, because this no longer goes beyond it.
On the other hand, however, it posits that object rather outside itself, as a beyond of itself.
But this being-in-and-for-itself is likewise posited as one which is not free of self-consciousness, but is for the sake of the latter and through it.
zh: 在道德世界观中，我们一方面看到意识自己是有意识地产生出它的对象；我们看到它既不把这个对象当作一个外在之物碰上，也不是对它失去意识，而是它处处依据一个根据，由这个根据设定出那个对象性的本质；因此它把这个对象当作自己本身来认识，因为它知道自己就是那个产生出它的能动者。
这样看来，它在这里似乎得到了安宁和满足，因为只有在它不必再超出自己的对象、而这个对象也不再超出它的地方，它才能找到这种安宁和满足。
但在另一方面，它自己毋宁是把那个对象设定到自己之外，设定为自己的彼岸。
但这个自在自为者同样地被设定为这样一个存在者：它并不脱离自我意识而自由，而是为了自我意识、并且通过自我意识才存在。

en: The moral world-view is therefore in fact nothing other than the development of this underlying contradiction in its various aspects; it is – to use a Kantian expression here, where it is most appropriate – a whole nest of thoughtless contradictions.

Consciousness behaves in this development in such a way that it fixes on a moment and passes immediately from there to the other, sublating the first; but once it has posited this second, it dissembles that same one again as well and rather makes the opposite into the essence.

At the same time it is aware of its contradiction and its dissembling; aware indeed, for it passes over from a moment immediately, in relation to this very moment itself, to the opposite; because a moment has no reality for it, it posits precisely that same moment as real, or – which is the same thing – in order to assert a moment as being in itself, it asserts the opposite as the in-itself-existent.
It thereby confesses that in fact it is in earnest about none of them.
This is to be considered more closely in the moments of this dizzying movement.
zh: 所以道德世界观实际上无非就是那个处在底层的、作为根据的矛盾向各个方面的展开；它——在这里最恰当地借用一个康德的说法——就是一整窝不动脑筋的矛盾。
意识在这种展开中是这样行事的：它抓住一个环节，随即从那里直接转到另一个环节，把第一个扬弃掉；可是等它把这个第二个设定起来之后，它同样又把这个东西伪装起来，毋宁是把对立面当成了本质。
同时它也明知自己的矛盾和自己的伪装；而且是明知的，因为它从一个环节出发，就这个环节本身直接转到它的对立面；因为一个环节对它来说没有实在性，它就恰恰把这个环节设定为实在的；或者说，这是一回事：为了把一个环节断言为自在地存在着的，它反而把对立面断言为那个自在存在者。
它就这样承认：它对其中任何一个实际上都不是当真的。
这一点得在这令人眩晕的运动的诸环节中更仔细地看一看。

en: Let us first leave to itself the presupposition that there is an actual moral consciousness, because it is not made immediately in relation to anything preceding, and let us turn to the harmony of morality and nature, the first postulate.
It is to be in itself, not for the actual consciousness, not present; rather, presence is only the contradiction of the two.
In presence, morality is assumed to be there present, and actuality is so posited that it is not in harmony with it.
But the actual moral consciousness is an acting one; precisely in this lies the actuality of its morality.

But in the acting itself that position is immediately dissembled; for acting is nothing other than the actualization of the inner moral purpose, nothing other than the bringing-forth of an actuality determined through the purpose, or of the harmony of the moral purpose and actuality itself.

At the same time the completion of the deed is, for consciousness, the presence of this unity of actuality and purpose; and because in the accomplished deed consciousness realizes itself as this single one, or beholds determinate being returned into itself, and the enjoyment consists in this, that form of the moral purpose which is called enjoyment and happiness is at the same time contained in the actuality of the moral purpose.
– Acting therefore in fact immediately accomplishes that which was posited as not to occur and was only to be a postulate, only to be a beyond.
Consciousness therefore says through the deed that it is not in earnest about postulating, because the sense of acting is rather this: to bring to presence what is not supposed to be in presence.

And since for the sake of acting the harmony is postulated – what is namely to become actual through acting must be so in itself, otherwise actuality would not be possible –, the connection between acting and the postulate is of such a nature that for the sake of acting, that is, for the sake of the actual harmony of purpose and actuality, this harmony is posited as not actual, as a beyond.
zh: 我们先把“存在一个现实的道德意识”这个前提暂且搁在一边吧，因为它当下并不是针对某个更早的东西提出的；我们转而来看道德与自然的和谐，这就是第一个假设。
它应当在自在的意义上存在，不是为现实意识而存在，也不是在场；毋宁说，在场恰恰只是这两者的矛盾。
在场之中，道德被假定为在场存在着，现实性则被设定成这样：它与道德并不处于和谐之中。
但现实的道德意识是一个行动着的意识；它的道德的现实性恰恰就在这里。
但在行动本身之中，那种处境立即就被伪装掉了；因为行动无非是内在道德目的的实现，无非是那个由目的规定出来的现实性、或者说道德目的与现实性本身的和谐的产生。
同时，行动的实现对意识来说就是现实性与目的这一统一的在场；又因为在完成了的行动中，意识把自己实现为这个个别者，或者观照到定在返回到它之中，而享受正在于此，所以道德目的的那个被称为享受与幸福的形式，同时也包含在道德目的的现实性之中。
——所以行动实际上当场就实现了那个本来被设定为不该发生的东西，它本应只是一个假设，只该在彼岸。
所以意识通过行动表明，它对这种假设并不是当真的，因为行动的意义毋宁是：把本来不该在现在的东西弄到现在来。
而由于为了行动的缘故，和谐被假设——那个要通过行动成为现实的东西自在地必须如此，否则现实性就不可能——所以行动与这个假设之间的关联是这样一种情形：为了行动、也就是为了目的与现实性的现实和谐的缘故，这个和谐反倒被设定为不是现实的，被设定为在彼岸。

en: In so far as it acts, therefore, it is not in earnest about the inappropriateness of purpose and actuality in general; on the contrary, it seems to be in earnest about the acting itself.
But in fact the actual deed is only the deed of the single consciousness, hence itself only something single and the work of chance.

But the purpose of reason, as the universal purpose comprehending everything, is nothing less than the whole world; a final purpose which goes far beyond the content of this single deed and must therefore be placed above all actual acting whatsoever.
Because the universal good is to be carried out, no good at all is done.
But in fact the nullity of actual acting and the reality only of the whole purpose, which are now posited, are likewise dissembled in every direction.

The moral deed is not something accidental and restricted, for it has pure duty as its essence; this makes up the one whole purpose, and the deed, therefore, as the actualization of the same, is – despite all other restriction of its content – the accomplishment of the whole absolute purpose.

Or if actuality is again taken as nature, which has its own laws and is opposed to pure duty, so that duty cannot realize its law in it, then – since duty as such is the essence – in fact what is at stake is not the accomplishment of pure duty, which is the whole purpose; for that accomplishment would have not pure duty, but its opposite, actuality, as its purpose.

But again it is dissembled that what is at stake is not actuality; for according to the concept of moral acting, pure duty is essentially acting consciousness; thus acting is indeed to be done, the absolute duty is to be expressed in all of nature, and the moral law is to become natural law.
zh: 所以，就它在行动而言，它对目的与现实性之间的不合宜一般来说并不是当真的；相反，它对行动本身看起来倒是当真的。
但事实上，现实的行动只是单个意识的行动，因此它本身也只是单个的东西，是偶然的产物。
可是理性的目的，作为那个普遍的、包罗一切的目的，不小于整个世界；它是一个远远超出这单个行动之内容的终极目的，因此总的说来必须被设定在一切现实行动之上。
因为那个普遍的好要去付诸实行，所以什么好事也没有做。
但事实上，现在被设定起来的、现实行动的无意义和仅仅属于整个目的的那种实在性，同样又在所有方面被伪装掉了。
道德的行动并不是某种偶然和受限制的东西，因为纯粹义务是它的本质；这构成了唯一的一个完整目的，因此这一行动作为它的实现，尽管其内容在其他方面还受着限制，却是整个绝对目的的完成。
或者，如果又把现实性当作自然来看待，而自然有它自己的法则并且与纯粹义务相对立，以至于义务不能把自己的法则在自然中实现，那么——既然义务本身是本质——实际上要紧的就并不是纯粹义务（它就是整个目的）的完成；因为这种完成的目的毋宁不是纯粹义务，而是它的对立面，即现实性。
但“要紧的不是现实性”这一点又再次被伪装掉了；因为按照道德行动的概念，纯粹义务在本质上是行动着的意识；因此行动固然是应当去做的，绝对义务应当在全部自然中表达出来，道德法则应当成为自然法则。

en: So if we let this highest good count as the essence, then the consciousness is not serious about morality at all.
For in this highest good nature does not have a law other than the one morality has.
Thus moral acting itself falls away, for acting is only possible on the presupposition of something negative which is to be sublated by the action.
But if nature is in accordance with the moral law, then this law would indeed be violated by acting, by the sublation of what exists.
- So in that assumption it is admitted that as the essential condition such a one is acknowledged in which moral acting is superfluous and does not occur at all.

The postulate of the harmony of morality and actuality - a harmony which is posited through the concept of moral acting, that is, through bringing both into agreement - therefore also expresses itself from this side in this way: because moral acting is the absolute end, the absolute end is that moral acting should not exist at all.
zh: 那么，如果我们把这个最高的善当作本质，意识对道德就根本不是当真的。
因为在这个最高的善里，自然并不具有一个不同于道德所具有的法则。
于是，道德的行动本身就落空了，因为行动只有在以一个否定物为前提时才有的，而这个否定物是要由行动来扬弃的。
可是，如果自然与道德法则相合，那么这个法则就会被行动、被对存在者的扬弃所违反。
——所以，在那个假定中人们承认：作为本质的状态是这样的一个状态，其中道德的行动是多余的，根本不会发生。
道德与现实性之和谐的假定——一种要通过道德行动的概念、也就是通过把两者带到一致而来的和谐——因此也从这一方面这样表达出来：因为道德的行动是绝对目的，所以绝对目的就是道德的行动根本不存在。

en: If we put together these moments through which the consciousness rolled itself along in its moral representing, then it becomes clear that it again sublates each one in its opposite.
It starts out from the assumption that for it morality and actuality do not harmonize, but it is not serious about this, for in action the presence of this harmony is there for it.
But it is not serious about this acting either, since it is something individual; for it has so high an end, the highest good.
But this too is again only a dissemblance of the matter, for in it all acting and all morality would fall away.
Or rather, it is properly not serious about moral acting; what is the most desirable, the absolute, is that the highest good be carried out and moral acting be superfluous.
zh: 如果我们把意识在自己的道德表象中滚过的这些环节摆在一起，就清楚可见：它把每一个环节又都在自己的反面中扬弃掉了。
它出发时就假定：对它来说，道德与现实性并不和谐，但它对这一点并不当真，因为在行动中，对它来说这种和谐是当下就有的。
不过它对这个行动也不认真，因为这是某个个别的东西；它有那么高的目的，那就是最高的善。
但这又一次只是对事情本身的伪装，因为在这样的情形中，一切行动和全部道德都会落空。
或者说，它对道德的行动其实并不认真，最值得欲求的、绝对的东西乃是：最高的善得以实现，而道德的行动是多余的。

en: From this result the consciousness must roll itself onward in its contradictory movement and must necessarily again dissemble the sublation of moral acting.
Morality is the in-itself; that it should hold its ground cannot be the accomplished final end of the world; rather the moral consciousness must be for itself and find a nature opposed to it.
But it must be completed in itself.
This leads to the second postulate of the harmony of itself and nature, which is immediately in it, the sensuous.
The moral self-consciousness posits its end as pure, as independent of inclinations and drives, so that it has annihilated in itself the ends of the sensuous.
- Yet this posited sublation of the sensuous essence it again dissembles.

It acts, brings its end to actuality, and the self-conscious sensuous, which is supposed to be sublated, is precisely this middle term between pure consciousness and actuality - it is the instrument of the former for its realization, or the organ and that which is called drive, inclination.
It is therefore not serious about the sublation of the inclinations and drives, for they themselves are the self-realizing self-consciousness.
But they are not to be suppressed either, but only to be in accordance with reason.

They are in accordance with it too, for moral acting is nothing other than the self-realizing consciousness, that is, the consciousness which gives itself the shape of a drive; that is, it is immediately the present harmony of drive and morality.
But in fact the drive is not only this empty shape which could have in itself another spring than it itself is and be driven by it.
For the sensuous is a nature which has its own laws and springs in itself; morality therefore cannot be serious about being the spring of the drives, the inclination-angle of the inclinations.

For since these have their own fixed determinacy and their own peculiar content, the consciousness to which they corresponded would rather be in accordance with them; an accordance which the moral self-consciousness forbids itself.
The harmony of both is therefore only in itself and postulated.

- In moral acting the present harmony of morality and the sensuous was just now posited, but this is now dissembled; it lies beyond consciousness in a misty distance in which nothing can any longer be exactly distinguished nor comprehended; for it did not succeed with the comprehension of this unity which we just now attempted.
- But in this being-in-itself the consciousness gives itself up entirely.
This being-in-itself is its moral completion, in which the struggle of morality and the sensuous has ceased and the latter is in accordance with the former in a way which cannot be grasped.

- That is why this completion too is again only a dissemblance of the matter, for in truth it would rather be morality itself that gives itself up in it, for morality is only the consciousness of the absolute end as of the pure one, thus in opposition to all other ends; it is just as much the activity of this pure end as it is conscious of the elevation above the sensuous, of the mixing-in of the sensuous, and of its opposite and of its struggle with morality.

- That the consciousness is not serious about its moral completion it expresses itself directly in this, that it dissembles it away out into infinity, that is to say, it asserts it as never completed.
zh: 从这个结果出发，意识必须在它自相矛盾的运动中继续向前滚动，并且必然要再次伪装对道德行动的扬弃。
道德是自在；它能够成立，这一点不可能是世界终极目的的完成；毋宁说，道德意识必须是自为的，并且发现一种与它相对立的自然。
但它本身必须得到完成。
这就导致了它与自然之和谐的第二个假定，而这自然在它身上是直接存在的，也就是感性。
道德的自我意识把它的目的设定为纯粹的、设定为不依赖偏好与冲动的东西，于是它就在自身中把感性的诸目的消灭掉了。
——可是，它又把这样建立起来的对感性本质的扬弃伪装掉了。
它行动着，把自己的目的带进现实；而那个本应被扬弃的、自我意识着的感性，恰恰就是纯粹意识与现实性之间的这个中项——它就是前者用来实现自己的工具，或者说是那个叫做冲动、叫做偏好的器官与东西。
因此它对扬弃偏好和冲动并不认真，因为恰恰它们就是那个现实化着自己的自我意识。
可是它们也不该被压抑，只是应当与理性相合罢了。
它们也确实与理性相合，因为道德的行动无非就是那个现实化着的、也就是给自己以冲动这一形态的自我意识，换句话说，它当下就是冲动与道德的和谐。
但事实上，冲动并不只是这个空洞的形态——它可以在自己身上装上另一个不同于它自己的发条，并且由那个发条推动。
因为感性是一种自然，它自己身上就带着自己的法则和自己的发条；所以道德也不可能当真去充当这些冲动的发条、这些偏好的倾斜角度。
因为既然这些冲动和偏好有自己固定的規定性和特有的内容，那么与它们相合的意识反倒会与它们相合；这样一种相合，正是道德的自我意识不容许自己有的。
所以两者的和谐只在自在之中，并且只是一个假定。
——刚才在道德的行动中，道德与感性的当下和谐被建立起来了，可是现在它被伪装掉了；它已经在意识之外，落在一片朦胧的远处，那里再也没有什么能分辨清楚、也再没有什么能把握得住；因为刚才我们试着去把握这一统一，却并没有成功。
——可是在这种自在之中，意识干脆就放弃了自己。
这种自在就是它的道德完成，在其中道德与感性的斗争停止了，而后者以一种无法把握的方式与前者相合。
——所以这一完成又一次只是对事情本身的伪装，因为事实上，在她之中毋宁是道德自己放弃了自己；因为道德不过是对绝对目的、即对纯粹目的的意识，也就是对一切其他目的处于对立之中的意识；它既是对这个纯粹目的的活动，又对那种超越感性的提升、感性的掺入，以及感性的对立面和它与道德的斗争有所意识。
——意识自己对道德的完成并不当真，这一点它就直接表达在：它把这一完成推到无限远处去伪装，也就是说，它断言这一完成从来没有完成过。

en: Rather, then, only this intermediate state of non-completion is valid for it – a state which yet is supposed at least to be a progression towards completion.
Yet it cannot be this either, for a progression in morality would rather be a move towards its ruin.
For the goal would be that aforementioned nothingness, the sublation of morality and of consciousness itself; but coming ever closer to the nothingness means diminishing.
Besides, progressing at all would just as much as diminishing admit differences of magnitude within morality; yet of these there can be no question in it.

In it, as in the consciousness for which the moral purpose is the pure duty, one cannot think of any diversity at all, and least of all of the superficial one of magnitude; there is only one virtue, only one pure duty, only one morality.
zh: 所以对它来说，有效的反而只是这种未完成的中间状态——不过这个状态毕竟应当至少是一种向完成的推进。
可它也不能是这，因为道德上的进展反而是走向道德本身的消亡。
因为目标就是前面说的那个虚无，也就是道德和意识本身的扬弃；而越来越接近虚无，就叫减少。
而且，进展本身和减少一样，都会在道德里容下量上的差别；可在道德里根本谈不上这些差别。
在道德里——在这个把道德的目的当作纯粹义务的意识里——根本不该设想有任何差异，最不该设想的就是量上那种表面的差异；这里只有一种德行，只有一个纯粹义务，只有一种道德。

en: Since, then, the moral consciousness is not in earnest about moral completion but rather about the intermediate state, that is, as has just been expounded, about non-morality, we thus return from another side to the content of the first postulate.
For it is not conceivable how happiness is to be demanded by this moral consciousness on the score of its desert.

It is conscious of its own incompleteness and can therefore not in truth demand happiness as a merit, not as something of which it would be worthy, but demand it only from a free grace, that is, demand happiness as such in and for itself, and not expect it from that absolute ground but according to chance and arbitrariness.
– Non-morality says precisely in this what it is, – that the point is not morality but happiness in and for itself, without any relation to the former.
zh: 既然这个道德意识对道德的完成并不认真，反倒认真对待中间状态，也就是像刚才所阐明的那样，对待非道德，那么我们就从另一个方面回到了第一个要求的内容。
因为无从看出，这个道德意识凭什么配得去要求幸福。
它知道自己尚未完成，因此实际上不能把幸福当作功劳去要求，不能把它当作自己配得的东西去要求，而只能从一种自由的恩赐中要求它，也就是说，把自在自为的幸福本身当作这样的东西去要求，而不是从那个绝对的根据去期待它，而是听凭偶然和任性去期待。
——非道德恰恰在这里表明了自己是什么：要紧的不是道德，而是自在自为的、与道德不相干的幸福。

en: Through this second aspect of the moral world-view the other assertion of the former is sublated as well, the one in which the disharmony of morality and happiness is presupposed.
– For the experience meant to be made is that in this present things go badly with the moral and, on the contrary, often well with the immoral.

Yet the intermediate state of incomplete morality, which has turned out to be the essential point, evidently shows that this perception and supposed-to-be experience is only a dissemblance of the matter.
For since morality is incomplete, that is, morality in truth is not there, what can be meant by the experience that things fare badly with it?

– Since it has at the same time emerged that the point is happiness in and for itself, it becomes evident that in judging that things go well with the immoral, no wrong is meant that would obtain here.
The designation of an individual as an immoral one falls away of its own accord, since morality at all is incomplete, and so has only an arbitrary ground.
The sense and content of the judgment of experience is thereby simply this, that happiness in and for itself should not accrue to some, that is, it is envy which takes morality as its cloak.
But the ground why the so-called happiness should be allotted to others is the good friendship which grants them and itself this grace, that is, this chance, and wishes it them.
zh: 通过道德世界观的这第二个方面，前者的另一个断言也被扬弃了，即那个预设了道德与幸福不和谐的断言。
——因为人们想要得到的经验是：在眼下这个时代，讲道德的往往过得不好，反倒是不讲道德的往往很走运。
可是，未完成的道德的这个中间状态既然已经显露出才是本质所在，就显然表明：这种知觉和自以为是的经验，不过是对事情的一种伪装。
因为道德既然是没有完成的，也就是说，道德实际上并不存在，那么说它过得不好这种经验又算什么呢？
——既然同时也已经显明，要紧的是自在自为的幸福，那么就可以看出，在评判不道德的人过得好这件事上，并不曾犯下什么不正当的行为。
既然道德总体上尚未完成，把一个个体称作不道德的说法就自行落空了，因此它只有一个任性的根据。
这样一来，经验判断的意义和内容就仅仅是：有些人本不该得到自在自为的幸福，也就是说，这是嫉妒，嫉妒拿道德当作自己的幌子。
但别人为什么反倒该得到所谓的幸福呢？根据就是那份交情，这份交情愿意把这份额外的恩赐、也就是这份偶然赐给他们，同时也留给自己。

en: The morality, then, in moral consciousness is incomplete; this is what is now put forward.
But it is its essence to be only the complete, the pure; the incomplete morality is therefore impure, or it is immorality.
The morality itself is thus in an essence other than the actual consciousness; it is a holy moral lawgiver,

– Morality, which is incomplete in consciousness and which is the ground of this postulating, first has the significance that morality, in that it is posited as actual in consciousness, stands in relation to an Other, to a determinate being, and so itself acquires being-other or difference, through which a manifold multiplicity of moral precepts arises.
But moral self-consciousness at the same time holds these many duties to be inessential; for it is only a matter of the one pure duty, and for it they have no truth insofar as they are determinate.
They can therefore have their truth only in an Other, and are – what they are not for it – holy through a holy lawgiver.
– Yet this too is again only a dissemblance of the matter.
For moral self-consciousness is to itself the Absolute, and duty simply only what it knows as duty.
But it knows only the pure duty as duty; what is not holy for it is not holy in itself, and what is not holy in itself cannot be sanctified through the holy being.

In general moral consciousness is not earnest about having something sanctified through a consciousness other than the one it itself is; for what is simply holy for it is only what is holy to it through itself and in it.
– It is no more earnest, then, about this other being being a holy one, for in it something is supposed to attain essentiality which has no essentiality for moral consciousness, that is, in itself.
zh: 所以，道德意识中的道德是没有完成的；现在提出来的正是这一点。
但道德的本质就是只做那个完成了的、纯粹的东西；没有完成的道德因此就是不纯粹的，或者说，它就是非道德。
所以道德本身是在另一个本质里，而不是在现实的意识里；它是一个神圣的道德立法者，
——在意识中尚未完成的道德，是这种设定的根据；它首先意味着：道德既然在意识里被当作现实的东西设下，它就处在与他者、与一个定在的关系中，因而它自身也就带上了他在、也就是那差别，由此产生出多种多样的道德诫命。
可是道德的自我意识同时又认为这许多义务是不本质的；因为它只关心那一个纯粹的义务，而对它来说，这些义务只要是特定的，就没有真理。
所以这些义务的真理只能在另一个他者那里才有，而它们——对道德的自我意识来说并不是这样——是靠一个神圣的立法者才成为神圣的。
——可是，这本身又不过是对事情的一种伪装。
因为道德的自我意识对自己而言就是绝对者，而义务就只是它所知道为义务的东西。
可是它只把那一个纯粹的义务当作义务；凡对它来说不神圣的，在自在意义上就不神圣，而凡在自在意义上不神圣的，就不能靠那个神圣的本质被神圣化。
总之，道德意识并不认真去让什么东西通过一个不同于它自己的意识而变得神圣；因为对它来说唯一神圣的，只是那个通过它自己、并且在它里面才是神圣的东西。
——所以它对这个另一个本质是不是神圣的同样并不认真，因为在这个本质里本应有某种东西取得实质性，而这种东西对道德的自我意识来说，也就是自在而言，是没有实质性的。

en: If it has been postulated of the holy essence that in it duty would have its validity not as pure duty but as a multiplicity of determinate duties, then this must in turn be dissembled, and the other essence alone is holy insofar as only pure duty has validity in it.
In fact, pure duty has its validity only in another essence, not in the moral consciousness.
Even though in it pure morality alone seems to prevail, this must nevertheless be posited otherwise, for it is at the same time natural consciousness.

Morality is in it affected and conditioned by sensuousness, hence not in and for itself but a contingency of the free will; in it, however, as pure will, a contingency of knowing; morality in and for itself is therefore in another essence.
zh: 如果说神圣的本体被设定为：义务在它里面不是作为纯粹的义务、而是作为许多特定的义务才有其有效性，那么这个本体就还得被伪装起来，而另一个本体只有在于其中只有纯粹的义务才有效时，才是神圣的。
其实，纯粹的义务只有在另一个本体里才有有效性，而不是在道德意识里。
尽管在它里面似乎只有纯粹的道德才算数，这一点还是得另作设定，因为它同时也是自然意识。
道德在其中受感性影响，并以感性为条件，所以不是自在自为的，而是自由意志的一种偶然性；但在它这个纯粹的意志中，道德又是知识的一种偶然性；因此，自在自为的道德是在另一个本体里。

en: This essence is therefore here pure completed morality, precisely because in it morality does not stand in relation to nature and sensuousness.
But the reality of pure duty is its actualization in nature and sensuousness.

The moral consciousness posits its imperfection in the fact that in it morality has a positive relation to nature and sensuousness, since for it this counts as an essential moment of morality, that morality has simply only a negative relation to nature and sensuousness.
The pure moral essence, on the contrary, because it is lifted above the struggle with nature and sensuousness, does not stand in a negative relation to them.
In fact, therefore, only the positive relation to them remains for it, i.e. precisely that which a moment ago counted as the uncompleted, as the immoral.

But pure morality entirely separated from actuality, so that it would equally have no positive relation to it, would be an unconscious, unreal abstraction in which the concept of morality, of thinking the pure duty and being a will and an action, would be simply sublated.
This so purely moral essence is therefore again a dissemblance of the matter and has to be given up.
zh: 所以这个东西在这里之所以是纯粹完成了的道德，正因为道德在它里面并不与自然和感性处在关系中。
但纯粹义务的实在性就是它在自然和感性中的实现。
道德意识把自己的不完善设定在这一点上：在它里面，道德对自然和感性有一种正的关系，因为对它来说，这就算作道德的一个本质环节，即道德对自然和感性干脆只是一种负的关系。
相反，纯粹的道德本质由于高出于同自然和感性的斗争，并不与它们处在负的关系中。
所以事实上留给它的就只有对它们的正的关系，也就是刚刚被视为未完成的、被视为不道德的那个东西。
但纯粹的道德如果完全与现实性分开，以致它同样也不再与现实性有正的关系，那就是一种没有意识的、不现实的抽象；在这种抽象中，道德的概念、纯粹义务的思考以及成为一个意志和一个行动，都被干脆地扬弃了。
所以这个如此纯粹道德的本体又是事情本身的一种伪装，必须被放弃。

en: But in this purely moral essence the moments of the contradiction, in which this synthetical representing moves about, and the opposite manifestations, which it lets succeed one another without ever bringing these its thoughts together and always lets one opposite succeed the other, approach each other so closely that consciousness must here give up its moral world-view and retreat into itself.
zh: 可是在这个纯粹道德的本体里，矛盾的那些环节（这种综合的表象就在其中打转），以及那些相反的表现——意识不把这些思想合拢起来，任它们一个接一个相继，总让一个相反者顶替另一个——彼此靠得如此之近，以致意识在这里必须放弃自己的道德世界观，退回到自身之中。

en: It therefore recognizes its morality as not completed, because it is affected by a sensuousness and nature opposed to it, which partly obscures morality itself as such, partly gives rise to a multiplicity of duties through which it gets into embarrassment in the concrete case of actual action; for every case is the concretion of many moral relations, just as an object of perception is generally a thing of many properties; and since the determinate duty is an end, it has a content, and its content is a part of the end, and morality is not pure.
– It therefore has its reality in another essence.
But this reality means nothing other than that morality is here in and for itself, — for itself, i.e. the morality of a consciousness, in itself, i.e. that it has determinate being and actuality.

– In that first uncompleted consciousness morality is not carried through; there it is the in-itself in the sense of a thing of thought; for it is bound up with nature and sensuousness, with the actuality of being and of consciousness, which make up its content, and nature and sensuousness are what is morally null.
– In the second, morality is present as completed and not as an unperformed thing of thought.

But this completion consists precisely in the fact that morality has in a consciousness actuality as well as free actuality, determinate being in general; that it is not the empty but the fulfilled, the rich in content; — i.e. the completion of morality is posited in this, that what a moment ago was determined as what is morally null is present in it and as its property.

It is to have validity simply as the unreal thing of thought of pure abstraction, but at the same time in this way to have no validity; its truth is to consist on the one hand in being opposed to actuality and being quite free and empty of it, and again in being actuality.
zh: 所以它认识到自己的道德并没有完成，因为它受一种与它对立的感性和自然所影响；这种感性和自然有时使道德本身作为道德变得晦暗，有时又产生出大批义务，而在实际行事的具体情形中，它就因这些义务而陷入困窘；因为每一个情形都是许多道德关系的具体化，正如一般说来知觉的一个对象是一个具有许多属性的物；而且既然特定的义务是目的，它就有内容，它的内容是目的的一个部分，道德因此并不纯粹。
– 于是道德在另一个本体中有它的实在性。
但这一实在性无非意味着：道德在这里自在自为，——自为，即是一个意识的道德；自在，即它有定在、有现实性。
– 在那第一个未完成的意识里，道德并没有被执行出来；在它里面，道德是作为思想之物的自在；因为它同自然和感性、同存在和意识的现实性结合在一起，而这些构成了它的内容，而自然和感性就是在道德上无足轻重的东西。
– 在第二个意识里，道德是作为完成了的道德而存在的，而不是作为一种未执行的思想之物。
但这一完成恰恰在于：道德在一个意识中具有现实性以及自由的现实性，总之具有定在；它不是空无，而是那个被充实了的、充满内容的东西；——也就是说，道德的完成被设定在于：刚才被定为在道德上无足轻重的东西，存在于道德之中并附着于道德。
道德这一方面要干脆只作为纯粹抽象的、不现实的思想之物才有有效性，另一方面同样在这一方式下又并不具有有效性；它的真理要在于：一面与现实性相对立，完全脱离现实性、是空无的，另一面又在于它就是现实性。

en: The syncretism of these contradictions, which is laid out in the moral world-view, collapses into itself, in that the difference on which it rests, from such a difference as must necessarily be thought and posited and yet is at the same time inessential, becomes a difference which no longer even lies in the words.

What at the end is posited as a something distinct, both as the null and as the real element, is one and the same thing, determinate being and actuality; and what absolutely shall be the null only as the beyond of actual being and consciousness, and equally only in it and as a beyond, is the pure duty and the knowing of it as the essence.

The consciousness that makes this difference, which is no difference, saying of actuality that it is at once the null and the real, saying of pure morality that it is at once the true essence and the essenceless, speaks out together the thoughts which it had previously separated, speaks out that it is not in earnest about this determination and this sundering of the moments of the self and of the in-itself, but rather that it keeps enclosed in the self of self-consciousness what it says to be the absolute, existing outside consciousness, and that what it says to be the absolutely thought or the absolute in-itself it takes precisely for that which does not have truth.
– It becomes clear to consciousness that the sundering of these moments is a dissemblance, and it would be hypocrisy if it still maintained it.

But as moral pure self-consciousness it flees from this inequality of its representing; with that which its essence is, out of this untruth, which declares true what counts for it as untrue, it retreats into itself with disgust.

It is pure conscience, which scorns such a moral world-representation; it is in itself the simple, self-certain spirit, which without the mediation of those representations acts immediately and conscientiously, and in this immediacy has its truth.

– But if this world of dissemblance is nothing other than the development of moral self-consciousness in its moments and thereby its reality, then through its retreat into itself it becomes in terms of its essence nothing other; its retreat into itself is rather only the attained consciousness that its truth is a presupposed one.

It would still have to profess it as its truth, for it would have to express and present itself as an objective representation, while knowing that this is only a dissemblance; it would thus in fact be the hypocrisy, and that scorn of that dissemblance already the first expression of the hypocrisy.
zh: 道德世界观中被铺展开来的这些矛盾的这种混同，其自身坍塌了，因为：它所依托的那个差别——即那种必然地被思考、被设定，却又同时是不本质的差别——变成了一个连词句里都不再存在的差别。
最终被设定为一个彼此有别的东西，无论是作为无足轻重之物还是作为实在物，其实是一个而且就是同一个东西，即定在和现实性；而那个绝对地、仅仅作为现实的存在与意识的彼岸、并且同样只在这个彼岸之中而作为一个彼岸才应当算作无足轻重之物的，就是纯粹的义务以及对这一义务作为本质的知识。
作出这个其实并不存在的差别、把现实性同时说成无足轻重之物和实在之物、把纯粹的道德同样说成真正的本质和没有本质的东西的那个意识，把它先前分开的思想一齐说出，也说出：它对这种规定和把自我与自在这两个环节分开并不认真，而是把它所说的那个作为绝对者、作为在意识之外存在的东西，收在自我意识的自我之中不放；而它所说的那个绝对被思想的东西或绝对的自在，正因为如此，它才当作没有真理的东西。
– 意识会看出，把这些环节分开乃是一种伪装；如果它仍然保持着这种分开，那就是虚伪。
可是，作为道德的纯粹自我意识，它逃离自己表象活动的这种不均衡；连同它本质之所是，它带着厌恶从这种不真理（这种不真理把对它而言不真的东西说成真）退回到自身之中。
它是纯粹的良心，鄙弃这样一种道德的世界表象；它在自身之中就是那个简单的、对自身有确定性的精神，它不经由那些表象的中介，直接凭良心行事，并且在这种直接性中拥有它的真理。
– 但是，如果这个伪装的世界无非是道德自我意识在其各个环节中的发展，因而就是它的实在性，那么它由于退回自身之中，按其本质并不会变成别的什么东西；它退回自身，倒只不过取得了这样一个意识：它的真理是预先设定好的。
它还是不得不把这一真理说成自己的真理，因为它不得不把自己说成、展示成一个对象的表象，却又知道这只是一种伪装；这样一来，事实上虚伪就在场了，而对那种伪装的鄙弃本身就已经是虚伪的第一个表现。

17.en: c. Conscience. The beautiful soul, evil and its forgiveness
17.zh: c. 良心。美的灵魂、恶与它的宽恕

en: The antithesis of the moral world-view, that there is a moral consciousness and that there is none, – or that the validity of duty is a beyond of consciousness and conversely takes place only in it, had been summed up into the representation in which the non-moral consciousness is taken to be moral, its accidental knowing and willing is taken to count for full weight, and happiness is granted to it by grace.
This self-contradictory representation the moral self-consciousness did not take upon itself, but transposed it into an essence other than itself.
But this setting-outside of itself of what it must think as necessary is just as much a contradiction in terms of form as that one is in terms of content.

But since in itself precisely that which appears as contradictory, and with which the moral world-view busies itself in separating and resolving again, is the same, namely that pure duty as pure knowing is nothing other than the self of consciousness and the self of consciousness [is] being and actuality, – just as what is to be the beyond of the actual consciousness is nothing other than pure thinking, thus in fact the self, so for us, or in itself, self-consciousness returns into itself and knows as itself that essence in which the actual is at once pure knowing and pure duty.
It itself is for itself the fully valid in its contingency, which knows its immediate individuality as pure knowing and acting, as true actuality and harmony.
zh: 道德世界观的这种二律背反——说有一个道德意识，又说没有道德意识，——或者说，义务的有效性是意识的彼岸，反过来又只在意识中才成立——曾经被概括在这样一种表象里：在其中，非道德的意识被当作道德的，它偶然的知识与意愿被当作完全算数，而幸福则是出于恩惠才落到它头上的。
这个自相矛盾的表象，道德的自我意识并没有挪到自己身上，而是把它移到了一个不同于它的本体之中。
但把那种它必须当作必然的东西放到自己之外，就形式而言同样是一种矛盾，正如前一个矛盾就内容而言是矛盾一样。
但自在地看，那显得自相矛盾的、道德世界观为之分分合合的东西，恰恰就是同一个东西：作为纯粹知识的纯粹义务无非就是意识的自我，而意识的自我[就是]存在和现实性；——同样，应当是现实意识的彼岸的东西，无非就是纯粹思维，也就是事实上就是自我；于是对我们来说，或者说自在地，自我意识就退回自身之中，并且把那个使现实者同时是纯粹知识和纯粹义务的本体认作自己。
它对自己就是那在其偶然性中完全有效的东西，它把自己的直接个别性知道为纯粹的知识与行动，知道为真正的现实性与和谐。

en: This self of the conscience, the spirit which is immediately certain of itself as the absolute truth and of being, is the third self that has become ours from the third world of spirit, and can briefly be compared with the previous ones.
The totality or actuality which presents itself as the truth of the ethical world is the self of the person; its determinate being is being-recognized.

As the person is the substance-empty self, so too is its determinate being the abstract actuality; the person counts, and that immediately; the self is the point that rests immediately in the element of its being; it is without the separation from its universality, so that both are therefore not in movement and in relation to one another; the universal is in it without distinction, is neither the content of the self nor is the self fulfilled through itself.
– The second self is the world of culture that has come to its truth, or the spirit of the split restored to itself, – absolute freedom.

In this self that first immediate unity of individuality and universality falls apart; the universal, which equally remains pure spiritual essence, being-recognized, or general will and knowing, is the object and content of the self and its universal actuality.
But it does not have the form of the determinate being free of the self; it therefore comes in this self to no fulfillment and to no positive content, to no world.
The moral self-consciousness does indeed let its universality free, so that it becomes a nature of its own, and equally it holds it fast within itself as sublated.
But it is only the dissembling play of the alternation of these two determinations.

As conscience it first has in its self-certainty the content for the duty which was empty before, as well as for the empty right and the empty general will; and [it has], because this self-certainty is equally the immediate, the determinate being itself.
zh: 良心的这个自我，这个直接地知道自己就是绝对真理、就是存在的精神，就是那个从精神的第三个世界中对我们而言成为我们的第三个自我；它可以同前面几个自我简略地比较一下。
那个作为伦理世界的真理而呈现自身的总体性或现实性，就是人格的自我；它的定在就是被承认。
人格是实体空无的自我，它的定在同样是抽象的现实性；人格是算数的，而且是直接地算数；自我是在其存在的元素中直接静止着的那一点；它没有同它的普遍性分离开来，因此两者都不处在运动中、也不彼此处在关系中；普遍者毫无区别地就在它里面，既不是自我的内容；自我也不是通过自身得到充实的。
——第二个自我就是达到了其真理的教养世界，或者说就是复归于自身的分裂的精神，——就是绝对自由。
在这个自我中，那第一个个别性与普遍性的直接统一就分解开了；而普遍者——它同样依旧是纯粹的精神本体、被承认，或者是一般的意志与知识——是自我的对象和内容，是它的普遍现实性。
但它并不具有那种脱离自我的定在的形式；因此它在这个自我中得不到任何充实，得不到任何肯定的内容，得不到任何世界。
道德的自我意识确实把它的普遍性放了自由，使它成为一个自己的本性；同样，它也把普遍性作为被扬弃的东西固定在自身之中。
但它不过是这两种规定彼此交替的伪装游戏。
作为良心，它首先在自己的自身确定性中有了内容：有了先前空着的义务的内容，也有了空的权利和空的一般意志的内容；而且［它］之所以有，是因为这种自身确定性同样就是直接者，就是定在本身。

en: Having reached this its truth, the moral self-consciousness therefore does not leave but sublates the separation within itself, out of which the dissemblance arose, the separation of the in-itself and the self, of pure duty as pure purpose and of actuality as a nature and sensuousness opposed to the pure purpose.

It is, thus returned into itself, concrete moral spirit, which does not, in the consciousness of pure duty, give itself an empty standard which would be opposed to the actual consciousness; but pure duty just like the nature opposed to it are sublated moments; it is moral essence actualizing itself in immediate unity, and the action is immediately the concrete moral shape.
zh: 达到了这个属于它的真理，道德的自我意识因此并不是离开自身内部的这种分离，而是扬弃它；伪装正是从这种分离中产生的，即自在与自我的分离、作为纯粹目的的纯粹义务与作为同纯粹目的相对立的那种本性和感性的分离。
这样退回自身之后，它就是具体的道德精神：它并不在对纯粹义务的意识中给自己立一个空的尺度，仿佛那尺度会同现实的意识相对立似的；相反，纯粹的义务以及与它相对立的那种本性，都是被扬弃的环节；它是在直接统一中把自己实现出来的道德本体，而行动则是直接具体的道德形态。

en: There is a case of acting present; it is an objective actuality for the knowing consciousness.
This as conscience knows it in an immediate concrete way, and it is at the same time only what it knows it to be.

The knowing is contingent insofar as it is other than the object; the spirit certain of itself, however, is no longer such a contingent knowing and creation of thoughts within itself, of thoughts from which the actuality would be different; but since the separation of the in-itself and the self is sublated, the case is immediately, in the sensuous certainty of knowing, what it is in itself, and it is in itself only as it is in this knowing.

– Acting as the actualization is thereby the pure form of the will; the mere inversion of actuality as a being case into an actuality done, of the mere manner of objective knowing into the manner of knowing the actuality as one brought forth by consciousness.

As sense-certainty is immediately taken up into the in-itself of spirit or rather is inverted, so this inversion too is simple and unmediated, a transition through the pure concept without a change of the content, which is determined by the interest of the consciousness that knows it.
– Conscience further does not sort the circumstances of the case into various duties.

It does not behave as a positive universal medium in which the many duties would each for itself hold fast an unmoved substantiality, so that either nothing at all could be acted, because every concrete case contains the opposition in general and as a moral case the opposition of duties, so that in the determination of acting one side, one duty, would always be violated, – or that if one acts, the violation of one of the opposed duties would actually occur.

Conscience is rather the negative One or absolute self which annihilates these different moral substances; it is simple duty-conforming acting, which does not fulfill this or that duty but knows and does what is concretely right.
It is therefore moral acting as such only in general into which the preceding actionless consciousness of morality has passed over.

– The concrete shape of the deed may by the distinguishing consciousness be analyzed into various properties, i.e. here into various moral relations, and these may either each, as it must be if it is to be a duty, be declared to hold absolutely, or also be compared and examined.

In the simple moral action of conscience the duties are so scattered that all these individual essences are immediately cut off, and the testing shaking at the duty does not take place at all in the unshaken certainty of conscience.
zh: 这里有一个行动的情形；对知着的意识来说，它是一种对象性的现实性。
它作为良心以直接具体的方式知道这个情形，而与此同时，这个情形又恰恰只是它所知道的那个样子。
只要知识不同于对象，它就是偶然的；而那个对自身有确定性的精神则不再是这种偶然的知识，不再是在自身中创造那些不同于现实性的思想；相反，既然自在与自我的分离已被扬弃，这个情形就直接地在知识的感性确定性中就是它自在所是的样子，而它也只如它在这个知识中所是的那样自在。
——行动作为实现在这里就是意志的纯粹形式；它只是把作为现存情形的现实性反过来变成已做出的现实性，把对象性认识的那种单纯方式反过来变成对作为意识所做出来的现实性的认识的方式。
正如感性确定性直接地被纳入精神的自在、或者不如说被反转过来一样，这一反转同样简单而不经中介，是通过纯粹概念的一次过渡，内容并不改变，而内容是由那个知着它的意识的利害关系来规定的。
——良心也不把这个情形的种种情状分别归到不同的义务里去。
它并不表现为一个肯定的普遍媒介，在其中许多义务各自都能守住不动摇的实体性，以致要么根本不能行动，因为每一个具体情形都包含着对立本身，而作为道德情形还包含着义务的对立，因此在对行动的规定中总有一方、总有一项义务会被违反；——要么，一旦行动，违反其中一项相对立的义务就真的发生了。
良心毋宁是这个否定的一，或者绝对自我，它消灭这些不同的道德实体；它是单纯的合乎义务的行动，它并不履行这一项或那一项义务，而是知道并做出具体而言正确的那个东西。
所以，先前那个无行动的道德意识过渡过来的，正是道德的行动本身，就是行动本身。
——行动的具体形态可以由那个加以区分的意识分析成不同的属性，即在这里分析成不同的道德关系；而这些关系或者其中每一项——如果它应当是义务的话就必须如此——被说成绝对有效的，或者也被加以比较和检验。
在良心的单纯道德行动中，义务被泼洒得如此之远，以致所有这些单个本体都被直接截断，而那种对义务加以检验的摇撼，在良心的不动摇的确定性中根本不会发生。

en: Just as little is present in conscience that going-back-and-forth uncertainty of consciousness which at one time places the so-called pure morality outside itself into another holy essence and counts itself as the unholy, but at another time again places the moral purity within itself and the connection of the sensuous with the moral into the other essence.
zh: 同样，在良心中也没有那种意识来回摇摆的不确定性：这种意识时而把所谓的纯粹道德放到自身之外、放进另一个神圣的本体，并把自己看作不神圣的；时而又把道德的纯洁放到自身之内，把感性与道德的联结放进另一个本体。

en: It renounces all these positions and dissemblings of the moral world-view, in that it renounces the consciousness which takes duty and actuality to be contradictory.
According to the latter, I act morally, in that I am conscious that I am only fulfilling the pure duty and not anything else; which amounts in fact to saying that I am not acting at all.

But when I act in fact, I am conscious of something other, of an actuality which is already there and of one which I want to bring forth; I have a determinate end and fulfil a determinate duty; what is at work in it is something other than the pure duty, which alone was meant to be intended.

– Conscience, on the contrary, is the consciousness of the fact that, if the moral consciousness states pure duty as the essence of its action, this pure end is a dissemblance of the matter; for the matter itself is that pure duty consists in the empty abstraction of pure thought and has its reality and its content only in a determinate actuality, an actuality which is the actuality of consciousness itself and of the same not as a thing of thought but as of an individual.
Conscience has for itself its truth in the immediate certainty of itself.

This immediate concrete certainty of itself is the essence; viewed in accordance with the opposition of consciousness, the self's own immediate individuality is the content of the moral deed; and its form is precisely this self as pure movement, that is, as knowing or as the self's own conviction.
zh: 它放弃道德世界观的所有这些立场和伪装，因为它放弃了那种把义务与现实性看作彼此矛盾的意识。
照后一种看法，我是在道德地行事，因为我知道自己只是在履行纯粹的义务，而不是别的什么东西；这实际上就是说，我并没有在行事。
但当我真正行事时，我意识到的是别的东西，是已经在那里的现实性和我要使之产生的现实性；我有一个特定的目的是的，我履行一项特定的义务；这其中起作用的不是那唯一本应被追求的纯粹义务，而是别的东西。
– 良心倒是对下面这一点有意识：如果道德意识把纯粹的义务说成是自己行动的本质，那么这个纯粹的目的就是事情本身的一种伪装；因为事情本身就在于，纯粹的义务只在纯粹思想的空洞抽象中才成立，而它的实在性和内容只有在一种特定的现实性中才有；这种现实性是意识本身的现实性，意识不是作为思想之物、而是作为个别者才有这种现实性。
良心对自己来说，其真理在于它对自身的直接确定性。
这种对自身的直接具体的确定性就是本质；按照意识的那个对立来看，自我自身的直接个别性就是道德行动的内容；而它的形式恰恰就是这个自我，作为纯粹的运动，也就是作为知识、作为自身的确信。

en: Considering this more closely in its unity and in the meaning of its moments, the moral consciousness comprehended itself only as the in-itself or essence, but as conscience it comprehends its being-for-itself or its self.

– The contradiction of the moral world-view resolves itself, that is, the difference underlying it shows itself not to be a difference, and it runs together into pure negativity; but this negativity is precisely the self: a simple self, which is just as much pure knowing as knowing of itself as this individual consciousness.

This self therefore makes up the content of what was previously an empty essence, for it is the actual, which no longer has the meaning of being a nature alien to the essence and independent under its own laws.
It is, as the negative of the difference of the pure essence, a content, and indeed a content which holds good in and for itself.
zh: 把这个东西就其统一性和各环节的意义更仔细地看，道德意识过去只把自己理解为自在、也就是本质，而作为良心，它才把自己的自为存在、也就是自己的自我理解为自身。
– 道德世界观的矛盾消解了，也就是说，作为其基础的差别表明自己并不是差别，而是归结为纯粹的否定性；但这种否定性恰恰就是自我：一个简单的自我，它同样既是纯粹的知识，也是自身作为这个个别意识的知识。
所以这个自我构成了先前那个空洞本质的内容，因为它是现实的东西，它不再有这样一种含义：是一种对本质而言陌生的、在自己的法则下独立不依于它的自然。
它作为纯粹本质之差别的否定项，是一个内容，而且是一个自在自为地成立的内容。

en: Further, this self as a pure knowing identical with itself is the simply universal, so that precisely this knowing, as its own knowing, as conviction, is duty.

Duty is no longer the universal which stands over against the self, but it is known not to have validity in this separation; it is now the law which is the self for the sake of the self, and not the self on account of the law.

Law and duty, however, have for that reason not only the meaning of being-for-itself but also that of being-in-itself, for this knowing is precisely the in-itself on account of its identity with itself.
This in-itself also separates itself in consciousness from that immediate unity with the being-for-itself; thus set over against the other, it is being, being for another.

– Duty itself is now known as a duty which the self has abandoned, as being only a moment; it has sunk down from its meaning of being absolute essence to a being which is not self, not being for itself, and so to being for another.

But this being for another remains an essential moment precisely for that reason, because the self as consciousness constitutes the opposition of the being-for-itself and the being for another, and now duty in its immediate actuality is no longer merely the abstract pure consciousness.
zh: 此外，这个自我作为一种纯粹、与自身相同的知识，就是绝对普遍的东西，所以恰恰这种知识，作为它自身的知识、作为确信，就是义务。
义务不再是那个与自我相对的普遍者，而是被知道在这种分离中并不具有有效性；它现在是那个法则，它是为了自我而成为自我，而不是由于它的缘故自我才成为自我。
但法则和义务因此并不只有自为存在的意义，同样也有自在存在的意义，因为这种知识正是由于它与自身相同，才是自在。
这个自在在意识中也从它与自为存在的那种直接统一里分开出来；这样对立起来时，它就是存在，就是为他存在。
– 义务本身现在被知道是一种被自我离弃的义务，只是环节而已；它从自己作为绝对本质的意义上沉落下来，沉落成一种不是自我、不是自为的存在，因而就是为他存在。
但这种为他存在恰恰因此仍是本质的环节，因为自我作为意识构成了自为存在与为他存在的对立，而现在义务在它直接现实的方面不再只是那个抽象的纯粹意识。

en: This being for another is therefore the substance which is in itself and which is differentiated from the self.
Conscience has not given up pure duty or the abstract in-itself; rather it is the essential moment, namely to comport oneself towards others as the universal.
It is the communal element of the self-consciousness, and this [self-consciousness] the substance in which the deed has subsistence and actuality; the moment of being recognized by the others.
Moral self-consciousness does not have this moment of being-recognized, of the pure consciousness which is there; and is thereby not at all acting, not at all realizing.
Its in-itself is for it either the abstract unreal essence or being as an actuality which is not spiritual.
But the existent actuality of conscience is one which is self, that is, the determinate being of which it is conscious, the spiritual element of being recognized.

Doing is therefore only the translation of its individual content into the objective element in which it is universal and recognized; and precisely this, that it is recognized, makes the action an actuality.

The action is recognized and thereby actual, because the determinate actuality is immediately bound up with the conviction or the knowing, or the knowing of its end is immediately the element of determinate being, which is universal recognition.

For the essence of the action, duty, consists in the conscience's conviction of it; this conviction is precisely the in-itself itself; it is the self-consciousness that is universal in itself, or the being-recognized, and with this the actuality.
What is done with the conviction of duty is therefore immediately something which has subsistence and determinate being.

There is therefore no longer any talk of the good intention not coming to pass, or of good being badly served; rather, what is known as duty accomplishes itself and comes to actuality, because precisely what accords with duty is the universal of all self-consciousness, what is recognized and hence what exists.
Separated and taken by itself, without the content of the self, however, this duty is being for another, the transparent, which only has the meaning of a wholly contentless being.
zh: 所以这种为他存在就是自在的、与自我相区别的实体。
良心并没有放弃纯粹的义务或那个抽象的自在；它倒是本质的环节，即作为普遍者而与他人相对待。
它是自我意识的共同元素，而这个自我意识就是那使行动在其中具有定在与现实性的实体；就是被他人承认的环节。
道德的自我意识并没有这种被承认的环节，并没有这种在此的纯粹意识；因此它根本不是行事的，根本不是实现着的。
它的自在对它来说要么是那个抽象的、不现实的本质，要么是作为一种并非精神的现实性而存在。
但良心的存在的现实性是这样一种：它就是自我，也就是意识所知道的那个定在，是被承认的精神元素。
所以行动所做的只是把它个别的内容翻译到那个对象的元素里，在那个元素中它是普遍的和被承认的；而恰恰是它被承认这一点，使这个行为成为现实性。
行为是被承认的、因而就是现实的，因为这种有定在的现实性直接与确信或知识联结在一起；或者说，对自身目的的知识直接就是定在的那个元素，也就是普遍的承认。
因为行为的本质、义务，就在于良心对它的那份确信；这份确信恰恰就是自在本身；它就是在自在的意义上普遍的那个自我意识，或者说就是被承认者，并由此而是现实性。
所以，凭着对义务的确信而做出的事情，直接就是一种有存在、有定在的东西。
所以这里已经不必再谈什么好的意图不能实现，或者好事落不到好结果；相反，那个被知道是义务的东西会自行完成并达到现实性，因为恰恰合乎义务的东西就是所有自我意识的普遍者，就是被承认者、因而就是存在者。
但分开来、单独来看，撇开自我的内容，这义务就是为他存在，就是那种透明的、仅仅具有一种空无内容的本体这一含义的东西。

en: If we look back at the sphere with which spiritual reality entered being at all, then the concept was that the articulation of individuality is being-in-and-for-itself.
But the shape which expressed this concept immediately was the honest consciousness which busied itself with the abstract matter itself.

This matter itself was there predicate; but in conscience it is first the subject which has posited in itself all the moments of consciousness, and for which all these moments — substantiality in general, external determinate being and the essence of thought — are contained in this certainty of itself.

Substantiality in general has the matter itself in ethical life, external determinate being in culture, the essence of thought knowing itself in morality; and in conscience it is the subject which knows these moments in itself.
If the honest consciousness only ever seizes the empty matter itself, then conscience, by contrast, wins it in the fulfilment which it gives it through itself.
It is this power that it knows the moments of consciousness as moments and, as their negative essence, rules over them.
zh: 如果我们回望精神的实在性最初进入存在时所凭借的那个领域，那么当时成立的概念就是：个体性的言说就是自在自为。
但直接表达这个概念的形态是诚实的意识，它围着抽象的事情本身打转。
在那里，这件事情本身还只是谓词；只有在良心里，它才第一次成为主体，它把意识的所有环节都设定在自身，而在它自身的这种确定性里，所有这些环节——一般意义上的实体性、外在的定在以及思维的本质——全都包含在内。
一般意义上的实体性在伦理中把握到这件事情本身，外在的定在在教养中，自知着的思维本质在道德中；而在良心里，它是那个知道这些环节就在自身的主体。
如果诚实的意识永远只能抓住空虚的事情本身，那么良心相反是在它的充实中把握住它，而这种充实是良心通过自身给予它的。
它之所以是这种力量，就在于它把意识的环节当作环节来知道，并且作为这些环节的否定性本质支配着它们。

en: If the conscience is considered in relation to the individual determinations of the opposition which appears in action, and its consciousness of the nature of the same, then it first behaves as knower towards the actuality of the case in which one is to act.

Insofar as the moment of universality lies in this knowing, it belongs to the knowing of conscientious action to comprehend the present actuality without any restriction, and so to know the circumstances of the case precisely and to take them into consideration.
But this knowing, since it knows universality as a moment, is therefore such a knowing of these circumstances as is conscious of not comprehending them or of not being conscientious in them.

The truly universal and pure relation of knowing would be a relation to something not opposed, a relation to itself; but action through the opposition which is essential in it relates itself to a negativity of consciousness, to an actuality which is in itself.

Against the simplicity of pure consciousness — of what is absolutely other or of multiplicity in itself — it is an absolute multiplicity of circumstances, which divides and spreads itself infinitely backwards into its conditions, sideways in their coexistence, forwards in its consequences,

– The conscientious consciousness is conscious of this nature of the matter and of its relation to it, and knows that it does not know the case in which it acts according to this demanded universality, and that its pretence of this conscientious weighing of all circumstances is null.

But this knowledge and consideration of all circumstances is not entirely absent; it exists only as a moment, as something which is only for others; and its incomplete knowing, because it is its knowing, counts for it as sufficient and complete knowing.
zh: 如果把良心放到与在行动中显现的那个对立面的各个规定的关系之中，并且就这些规定的本性来考察良心的意识，那么它首先是作为知者与那个必须去行动的情形之现实性相关。
既然普遍性这一环节就在这种知里，那么把当前这一现实性不加限制地整个包进来、因而精确地知道情形的种种情势并加以权衡，就属于合乎良心的行动之知。
但这种知既然把普遍性当作一个环节来知道，那么它对这些情势就是这样一种知：它自己知道，自己并没有把它们整个包进来，或者在其中并没有做到合乎良心。
知识的那种真正普遍而纯粹的关系，应当是对某个不对立者的关系、对它自身的关系；但通过那个本质上属于它的对立面去行动，所涉及的却是意识的一个否定项、一个自在的现实性。
与纯粹意识的单纯性——与绝对的他者或自在的多样性的单纯性——相对，它却是情势的绝对众多，它向后分入自己的条件，向侧旁分入自己的并存，向前分入自己的后果，无限地分裂并展开，
——这种合乎良心的意识知道，事情正具有这样的本性，也知道自己同它的关系；它知道，它并没有按这种被要求的普遍性去认识它所行动的那个情形，而且它关于对一切情势作这种合乎良心的权衡的声称是无效的。
不过，对一切情势的这种知和权衡并不是完全没有；它只是作为环节存在，只是某种只为他人的东西；而且它那不完整的知，因为它是它自己的知，在它看来就算作充分而完整的知。

en: In the same way it behaves with regard to the universality of the essence or the determination of the content through pure consciousness.
– The conscience which strides to act relates itself to the many sides of the case.
This case splits up, and likewise the relation of pure consciousness to it, whereby the multiplicity of the case is a multiplicity of duties.
– Conscience knows that it has to choose and to decide among them; for none is absolute in its determinacy or in its content, but only the pure duty.
But this abstraction has in its reality acquired the meaning of the self-conscious I.
The spirit certain of itself rests in itself as conscience, and its real universality or its duty lies in its pure conviction of duty.
This pure conviction is as empty as such as the pure duty, pure in the sense that nothing in it, no determinate content, is duty.

But action is to be done, it must be determined by the individual; and the spirit certain of itself, in which the in-itself has acquired the meaning of the self-conscious I, knows that it has this determination and content in the immediacy of its own certainty.
This certitude is, as determination and content, the natural consciousness, i.e. the drives and inclinations.
– Conscience recognizes no content as absolute for itself, for it is the absolute negativity of everything determinate.

It determines from out of itself; but the circle of the self within which determinacy as such falls is what is called sensibility; to have a content from the immediacy of its own certainty, nothing is at hand except it.

– Everything which in earlier shapes presented itself as good or evil, as law and right, is something other than the immediacy of its own certainty; it is a universal which is now a being for other; or viewed otherwise, an object which, mediating consciousness with itself, steps in between consciousness and its own truth and much rather separates consciousness from itself than that it should be its immediacy.

– But for conscience the certainty of itself is the pure immediate truth; and this truth is thus its own immediacy of self-certainty represented as content, i.e. altogether the arbitrariness of the individual and the contingency of its unconscious natural being.
zh: 对于本质的普遍性，或者对于纯粹意识对内容的规定来说，情况也是这样。
——大步走向行动的良心关联着这个情形的许多方面。
这个情形分解开来，纯粹意识与它的关系也同样分解开来；由此，情形的多样性就成了一种义务的多样性。
——良心知道，它得在这些义务之间加以选择和决定；因为其中没有哪一个在其规定性上或在其内容上是绝对的，绝对的只有纯粹的义务。
但这个抽象物在它的实在性中获得了自我意识的自我这一意义。
那个自身确定的精神作为良心安息在自身之中，而它的实在的普遍性、也就是它的义务，就在于它对义务的纯粹确信。
这种纯粹的确信作为这样的东西，和纯粹的义务一样空洞；它纯粹到这个意思：其中没有任何东西、没有任何特定的内容是义务。
可是必须行动，它必须由个体来规定；而那个自身确定的精神——自在在其中已经获得了自我意识的自我这一意义——知道，它在自身的直接确定性中就有这个规定和这个内容。
这种确定性作为规定和内容，就是自然的意识，也就是种种冲动和倾向。
——良心不把任何内容认作对自身来说是绝对的，因为它是规定的一切的绝对否定性。
它从自身出发去规定；而规定性作为规定性本身落入其中的那个自我的范围，就是所谓的感性；至于说从自身的直接确定性中取得一个内容，那么手边除了它之外一无所有。
——凡是先前诸形态中曾表现为善或恶、表现为法则与法的东西，都是不同于它自身那种直接确定性的他者；它是一个普遍者，这个普遍者现在是为他者的存在；或者换个角度看，它是一个对象，它把意识与意识自身中介起来，横插在意识与它自己的真理之间，因此与其说它是意识的直接性，不如说它把意识从自身那里分离开来。
——可是对良心来说，它自身的确定性就是纯粹而直接的真理；而这一真理于是就是它那被表象为内容的、直接的自身确定性，也就是总之说，个体的任性以及它那无意识的自然存在的偶然性。

en: This content counts at the same time as the moral essence or as duty.
For the pure duty is, as already turned out in the testing of the laws, utterly indifferent to every content and tolerates every content.

Here it at the same time has the essential form of being-for-itself, and this form of individual conviction is nothing else than the consciousness of the emptiness of the pure duty and of the fact that it is only a moment, that its substantially is a predicate which has its subject in the individual, whose caprice gives it the content and can bind any content to this form and affix its conscientiousness to it.

– An individual increases his property in a certain way; it is a duty that each one provide for the preservation of himself as well as of his family, and no less for the possibility of becoming useful to his fellow-men and of doing good to those in need of help.
The individual is conscious that this is duty, for this content is immediately contained in the certainty of itself; it further sees that it fulfills this duty in this case.
Others perhaps hold this certain way to be deception; they cling to other sides of the concrete case, but it holds fast to this side, in that it is conscious of the increase of property as pure duty.

– Thus what others call violence and wrong fulfills the duty of asserting one's independence against others; what they call cowardice fulfills the duty of preserving for oneself life and the possibility of being useful to one's fellow-men; but what they call bravery rather violates both duties.

But cowardice must not be so clumsy as not to know that the preservation of life and of the possibility of being useful to others are duties, – as not to be convinced of the dutifulness of its action and not to know that the dutiful consists in the knowing; otherwise it would commit the clumsiness of being immoral.

Since morality lies in the consciousness of having fulfilled duty, this will not be lacking to the action that is called cowardice any more than to that which is called bravery; the abstractum called duty is capable, like every one, of this content too, – it therefore knows what it does as duty, and in that it knows this and the conviction of duty is itself the dutiful, it is recognized by the others; the action thereby holds good and has actual determinate being.
zh: 这一内容同时被当作道德的本质或义务。
因为纯粹义务，正如在审查法则时已经呈现出来的那样，对任何内容都全然无所谓，并且容忍任何内容。
在这里，它同时具有自为存在的本质形式，而这种个体确信的形式不是别的，正是对纯粹义务之虚空的意识，也是对以下事实的意识：它只是环节，它的实体性是一个谓词，这个谓词在个体身上才有它的主体；个体的任性给它提供内容，能把任意一个内容系在这种形式上，并把它的良心性贴附其上。
——某个个体以某种方式增加他的财产；每个人都负有义务，既要照料他自身的保存以及他的家庭的保存，同样也要照料他得以对同类人有用、对需要帮助的人行善的可能性。
个体意识到，这就是义务，因为这一内容直接包含在对自身的确定性之中；它进一步看出，它在这种情况下履行了这一义务。
其他人也许把这种特定的方式当作欺骗；他们抓住具体情形的其他方面，而个体却由于意识到财产的增加就是纯粹义务，而紧紧抓住这一方面。
——所以，别人称之为暴行与不义的东西，履行了向他人坚持自己的独立性的义务；别人称之为怯懦的东西，履行了为自己保存生命、保存对同类人有用之可能性的义务；而别人称之为勇敢的东西，反倒违反这两种义务。
但怯懦可不能如此笨拙，以致于不知道保存生命和保存对他人有用的可能性是义务，——不能不相信自己行动的合义务性，也不能不知道合义务的东西就在于这种知道；否则，它就会犯下不道德这种笨拙。
由于道德就在于意识到已经履行了义务，所以这种意识对于被称为怯懦的行动，同对于被称为勇敢的行动一样，都不会缺少；被称为义务的抽象物，正如能容纳每一个内容一样，也照样能容纳这一内容，——所以它知道，它所做的就是义务；而由于它知道这一点，并且对义务的确信本身就是合义务的东西，所以它被其他人所承认；这一行为由此而有效，并具有现实的定在。

en: Against this freedom, which lays any arbitrary content into the universal passive medium of pure duty and knowing just as well as any other, it avails nothing to assert that another content should be laid in; for whatever content it be, each one bears on it the stain of determinacy, from which pure knowing is free and which it disdains, just as it can take up each one.
All content stands, in being a determinate one, on the same line with the other, even if it just seems to have the character that in it the particular is sublated.

It can seem that, in that in the actual case duty splits itself altogether into the opposition, and thereby into that of individuality and universality, that duty whose content is the universal itself thereby immediately has in it the nature of pure duty, and form and content hereby become wholly conformable to each other; so that, e.g., the action for the universal best would be preferred to that for the individual.

But this universal duty is altogether that which is present as substance existing in and for itself, as right and law, and holds independently of knowing and conviction as of the immediate interest of the individual; it is thus precisely that against whose form morality as such is directed.

But as regards its content, it too is a determinate one, insofar as the universal best is opposed to the individual; hereby its law is one such that conscience knows itself utterly free of it, and gives itself the absolute authorization to add to it and to take from it, to omit it as well as to fulfill it.
– Moreover, that distinction of duty against the individual and against the universal is, in accordance with the nature of opposition as such, nothing fixed.

Rather, what the individual does for himself also benefits the universal; the more he has provided for himself, the greater is not only his possibility of being useful to others, but his actuality itself is only this, to be and to live in connection with others; his individual enjoyment essentially has the meaning of thereby giving up his own to others and helping them to acquire their enjoyment.
In fulfilling the duty toward the individual, i.e. toward oneself, the duty toward the universal is also fulfilled.

– The consideration and comparison of duties, which would enter in here, would amount to the calculation of the advantage that the universal would have from an action; but partly morality would thereby fall prey to the necessary contingency of insight, partly it is precisely the essence of conscience to cut off this calculating and considering and, without such reasons, to decide out of itself.
zh: 针对这种自由——它把任意一个内容，正像另一个内容一样，放入纯粹义务与知识的普遍被动媒介之中——去主张应该放入另一个内容，是无济于事的；因为无论是什么内容，每一个都带着规定性的瑕疵；纯粹知识摆脱了这种规定性，对它不屑一顾，正如它能接纳任何一个一样。
一切内容，就其是一个特定的内容而言，都与另一个内容站在同一水平线上，哪怕它恰好显得具有这样的品格：在它之中，特殊的东西被扬弃了。
看起来可能如此：因为在现实的情形中，义务把自己分裂为对立，并由此分裂为个别性与普遍性的对立，所以那种以普遍者本身为内容的义务，就由此直接在自身具有纯粹义务的本性，形式与内容在这里就完全彼此相符了；因此，例如为普遍福利所做的行为，就应该优先于为个体福利所做的行为。
但这种普遍义务根本就是那样一种东西：它作为自在自为地存在着的实体、作为法与法则而现存，并且不依赖于知识、不依赖于确信，也不依赖于个别者的直接利益而有效；所以它恰恰就是道德一般而言所针对其形式的那种东西。
但就它的内容而言，它也是一个特定的内容，因为普遍福利是与个别者相对立的；于是，它的法则就成了这样一种法则：良心知道自己对它全然自由，并且给自己以绝对的权限，去对它有所增添、有所削减，去搁置它，也同样去履行它。
——此外，义务针对个别者与针对普遍者的那种区分，按照对立本身的本性来说，并不是什么固定的东西。
毋宁说，个体为自己所做的一切，也同样有益于普遍者；他越是为自己操办，不仅他有益于他人的可能性就越大，而且他自己的现实性本身也仅仅在于：与他人处于联系之中而存在和生活；他个别的享受本质上具有这样的意义：由此把属于自己的东西让给他人，并帮助他们获取他们的享受。
在履行对个别者、也就是对自己的义务时，对普遍者的义务也就同时得到了履行。
——这里会发生的对义务的斟酌与比较，会归结为对普遍者从某一行为中所获好处的计算；但这样一来，一方面，道德会由此落入洞见的必然偶然性之手，另一方面，斩断这种计算与斟酌、不凭这样的理由而由自身作出决断，恰恰正是良心的本质。

en: In this way conscience acts and maintains itself in the unity of being-in-itself and being-for-itself, in the unity of pure thinking and individuality, and is the spirit certain of itself, which has its truth in itself, in its self, in its knowing, and therein as the knowing of duty.

It maintains itself precisely thereby in this, that what is positive in the action – be it the content as well as the form of duty and the knowing of it – belongs to the self, to the certainty of itself; but what wants to step over against the self as its own in-itself counts as nothing true, only as sublated, only as moment.
Therefore it is not universal knowing as such that counts, but its acquaintance with the circumstances.

Into duty, as the universal being-in-itself, it lays the content which it takes from its natural individuality; for it is the one present in it itself; through the universal medium in which it is, this [content] becomes the duty which it exercises, and the empty pure duty is precisely thereby posited as sublated or as moment; this content is its sublated emptiness or the fulfillment.

– But conscience is likewise free from every content as such; it absolves itself from every determinate duty that is to count as law; in the strength of the certainty of itself it has the majesty of absolute autarky, to bind and to loose.

– This self-determination is therefore immediately the absolutely dutiful; duty is the knowing itself; but this simple selfhood is the in-itself; for the in-itself is pure self-equality, and this is in this consciousness.
zh: 这样，良心就在自在存在与自为存在的统一中、在纯粹思维与个体性的统一中行动并保持自身，它就是那种对自身有确定性的精神；这种精神在它自身那里、在它的自身中、在它的知识中，并且在这种知识作为关于义务的知识中，拥有它的真理。
它恰恰由此保持自身于这种统一之中：行为中积极的东西——无论是义务的内容、形式，还是对义务的知识——都归属于自身，归属于对自身的确定性；而凡是想要作为自身特有的自在而与自身相对立的东西，都算不得真的东西，只算作被扬弃的东西，只算作环节。
因此，有效的并不是一般的普遍知识，而是它对各种情势的了解。
它把从它的自然个体性中取来的内容放入义务这一普遍的自在存在之中；因为这个内容就是那种在它自身那里现存着的东西；通过这一内容存在于其中的普遍媒介，这一内容就成了它所实行的义务，而空洞的纯粹义务恰恰由此被设定为被扬弃的东西或环节；这一内容就是纯粹义务的被扬弃的虚空，或者说，就是充实。
——但良心同样对任何内容一般地都是自由的；它把自己从任何应当作为法则有效的特定义务中解脱出来；在对自身的确定性的力量中，它拥有绝对自足的威严，可以去束缚，也可以去释放。
——这种自我规定因此直接就是绝对合义务的东西；义务就是知识本身；但这种简单的自我性就是自在；因为自在就是纯粹的自身等同，而这种自身等同就在这种意识之中。

en: This pure knowing is immediately being for another, for as the pure self-equality it is the immediacy or the being.
But this being is at the same time the pure universal, the selfhood of all; or the acting is recognized and therefore actual.

This being is the element through which conscience stands immediately with all self-consciousnesses in the relation of equality; and the meaning of this relation is not the selfless law, but the self of conscience.
zh: 这种纯粹知识直接就是为他存在，因为作为纯粹的自身等同，它就是直接性，或者说，就是存在。
但这种存在同时又是纯粹的普遍者，是一切人的自我性；或者说，行动是被承认的，因而也是现实的。
这种存在是这样一个元素：良心通过它而与一切自我意识直接处于等同的关系之中；而这种关系的意义不是无自身的法则，而是良心的自身。

en: But in this, that this right which conscience does is at the same time a being-for-another, there seems to come upon it an inequality.
The duty it accomplishes is a determinate content; it is indeed the self of consciousness and therein its knowledge of itself, its equality with itself.

But once accomplished and placed into the universal medium of being, this equality is no longer knowing, no longer this distinguishing which just as immediately sublates its differences; rather, in being the difference is posited as abiding, and the deed is a determinate one, unequal to the element of the self-consciousness of all, hence not necessarily recognized.
Both sides, the acting conscience and the universal consciousness that recognizes this deed as duty, are equally free of the determinacy of this doing.

By virtue of this freedom, the relation in the common medium of connection is rather a relation of complete inequality; whereby the consciousness for which the deed is, finds itself in complete uncertainty about the acting, self-certain spirit.
He acts, he posits a determinacy as being; the others hold onto this being as to his truth and are therein certain of him; he has therein declared what counts for him as duty.
But he is free of any determinate duty; he is out beyond where they think he actually is; and this medium of being itself, and duty as being in itself, counts for him only as a moment.
What he thus sets before them, he again dissembles, or rather has immediately dissembled it.
For his actuality is to him not this duty and determination set forth, but that one which he has in the absolute certainty of himself.
zh: 不过，正因为良心所做的这种正当，同时是一种为他存在，一种不等同似乎就落到了它身上。
它所完成的义务是一个特定的内容；这个内容固然就是意识的自我，并因此是它对自身的知识、它与自身的等同。
可一旦完成、被置入存在的普遍媒介之中，这种等同就不再是知识，不再是那种同样直接扬弃其差别的区分了；相反，在存在中，差别被设定为持存着的，行动是一种特定的行动，与所有人的自我意识的元素不相称，因而并非必然被承认。
双方——行动着的良心和那个承认这一行动为义务的普遍意识——都同样不受这种行动的规定性的约束。
正因为这种自由，在这种相互联系的共同媒介中的关系，毋宁是一种完全的不等同关系；由此，行动为之而存在的那个意识，对行动着的、对自身确定的精神，就处在完全的不确定之中。
他行动，他把一种规定性设定为存在着的；其他人抓住这个存在，把它当作他的真理，并且在其中确信他；他由此说出了在他那里算作义务的东西。
可他不受任何特定义务的约束；他已经越出了他们以为他现实所在的地方；而这个存在媒介本身、以及作为自在存在者的义务，在他那里只算作一个环节。
所以他摆在他们面前的东西，他同样又加以伪装，或者毋宁说，已经直接把它伪装了。
因为他的现实性对他来说，并不是这种被摆出去的义务和规定，而是那种他在对自身的绝对确定性中才拥有的现实性。

en: So they do not know whether this conscience is morally good or evil, or rather they not only cannot know it, but must also take it for evil.
For just as it is free of the determinacy of duty and of duty as being in itself, so are they likewise.

What it sets before them, they themselves know how to dissemble; it is such that through it only the self of another is expressed, not their own; they know themselves not merely free of it, but must dissolve it in their own consciousness, annihilate it through judging and explaining, in order to preserve their self.
zh: 所以他们不知道，这个良心在道德上是善还是恶，或者毋宁说，他们不仅无法知道，而且还必须把它当作恶。
因为正如它不受义务的规定性、不受作为自在存在者的义务的约束一样，他们也同样如此。
它摆在他们面前的东西，他们自己也懂得加以伪装；它是一个这样的东西：通过它，只表达出别人的自我，而不是他们自己的自我；他们不仅知道自己对它不受约束，而且必须在他们自己的意识中把它消解掉，通过评判和解释把它化为乌有，以便保持他们自己的自我。

en: But the deed of conscience is not merely this determination of being that has been abandoned by the pure self.
What is to count and be recognized as duty is such only through the knowledge and the conviction of it as duty, through the knowledge of itself in the deed.
When the deed ceases to have this self upon it, it ceases to be that which alone is its essence.
Its determinate being, abandoned by this consciousness, would be a common actuality, and the deed would appear to us as an accomplishment of its pleasure and desire.

What is to have being here is essence only in that it is known as the individuality that expresses itself; and this being-known is what the recognized is, and what, as such, is to have determinate being.
zh: 不过，良心的行动并不仅仅是这种被纯粹自我抛弃了的存在的规定。
应当算作义务并被承认的东西，唯有通过关于它的知识、通过把它当作义务的确信，通过在行为中对自身的知识，才是这样的东西。
当行为不再把这个自我保持在自身之上的时候，它就不再是那个唯独构成它的本质的东西了。
它的定在，一旦被这种意识抛弃，就会是一种平庸的现实性，而行动在我们看来就会显现为对它的快乐和欲望的完成。
应当存在的东西，在这里唯有通过被知道为把自己表达出来的个体性，才成为本质性；而这种被知状态，正是那被承认的东西，并且作为这样的东西应当具有定在。

en: The self enters into determinate being as self; the spirit certain of itself exists as such for others; its immediate deed is not what counts and is actual; not the determinate, not the in-itself-being is the recognized, but only the self that knows itself, as such.

The element of abiding is the universal self-consciousness; what enters this element cannot be the effect of the deed; this does not hold out therein and obtains no continuance, but only self-consciousness is the recognized and wins actuality.
zh: 自我作为自我进入定在；对自身确定的精神作为这样的东西为他者而存在；它直接的行为不是那有效且现实的东西；被承认的不是那特定的东西，不是自在存在者，而唯独是知道自身的自我本身。
持存的元素是普遍的自我意识；进入这个元素的东西，不可能是行动的效果；这种效果在其中站不住脚，得不到任何持留，而唯独自我意识才是那被承认的东西，并且赢得现实性。

en: We hereby again see language as the determinate being of spirit.
It is the self-consciousness that is for others, which is immediately present as such and is as this universal.

It is the self that separates itself from itself, which as pure I = I becomes objective to itself, in this objectivity maintains itself just as much as this self as it immediately flows together with the others and is their self-consciousness; it apprehends itself just as it is apprehended by the others, and this apprehending is precisely the determinate being that has become self.
zh: 我们由此再次看到，语言是精神的定在。
它是为他者而存在的自我意识，它直接作为这样的东西当下在场，并作为这个普遍的东西而存在。
它是把自己同自身分离开来的自我，这个自我作为纯粹的 Ich = Ich 而对自己成为对象性的，在这种对象性中，它既保持自己为这个自我，又直接同他人汇流在一起、成为他们的自我意识；它听到自己，正如它被他人听到，而这种听到正是已经变成自我的定在。

en: The content that language has here won is no longer the inverted and inverting and torn self of the world of formation, but the spirit that has returned into itself, certain of itself and, in its self, of its truth or of its being recognized, and recognized as this knowing.

The language of the ethical spirit is the law and the simple command and the lament, which is more a tear over necessity; the moral consciousness, by contrast, is still mute, closed up with itself in its interior, for in it the self does not yet have determinate being, but determinate being and self first stand in an external relation to each other.

Language, however, emerges only as the middle of independent and recognized self-consciousnesses, and the existent self is immediately universal, manifold, and, in this manifoldness, a simple being-recognized.
The content of the language of conscience is the self that knows itself as essence.

This alone it speaks out, and this speaking-out is the true actuality of the doing and the validity of the deed. The consciousness speaks out its conviction; it is in this conviction alone that the deed is duty; and it also counts as duty solely in this, that the conviction is spoken out.

For the universal self-consciousness is free of the merely existent determinate deed; this counts for it as nothing as determinate being, but the conviction that it is duty—and this is actual in language.

– To actualize the deed means here not to translate its content from the form of the purpose or of being-for-itself into the form of abstract actuality, but from the form of the immediate certainty of itself, which knows its knowing or being-for-itself as the essence, into the form of the assurance that consciousness is convinced of the duty and, as conscience, knows the duty from itself; this assurance thus assures that it is convinced that its conviction is the essence.
zh: 语言在这里获得的内容，不再是教养世界的那个颠倒的、进行颠倒的、撕裂的自我，而是返回自身中的精神——这个精神对自身、并且在它的自我中对自身的真理或自身的被承认都确定无疑，并且作为这种知识而被承认。
伦理精神的语言是规律、简单的命令，以及那种更多地是对着必然性流下的一滴眼泪的悲叹；而道德意识却还是沉默的，封闭在自身之中、封闭在它的内里，因为在它那里，自我还没有定在，定在与自我彼此还只是处于一种外在的关系之中。
但语言只是作为独立的、被承认的自我意识的中项而显现出来，而定在着的自我直接就是普遍的、多重的，并且在这种多重性中，是一种简单的被承认状态。
良心的语言的内容，是把自身认作本质的自我。
它只把这说出来，而这种说出就是行动真正的现实性和行动的效力。意识说出它的确信；正是在这种确信中，行动才是义务；而行动也唯独因为这种确信被说出来，才算作义务。
因为普遍的自我意识不受那仅仅存在着的特定行动的约束；这种行动作为定在对它来说算不了什么，而唯独那种确信——即它是义务——才作数，而这种确信在语言中是现实的。
——实现行动，在这里并不是把行动的内容从目的或自为存在的形式翻译进抽象的现实性的形式，而是从对自身的直接确定性的形式——这种确定性把它的知识或自为存在认作本质——翻译进保证的形式，即保证意识对义务确信不疑、并且作为良心从自身知道义务；因此，这种保证所保证的，就是它确信它的确信就是本质。

en: Whether the assurance of acting from conviction of duty is true, whether what is done is really duty, — these questions or doubts have no sense against conscience.

– In that question whether the assurance is true, it would be presupposed that the inner intention is different from the professed one, i.e. that the willing of the single self could separate itself from duty, from the will of the universal and pure consciousness; the latter would be put into the speech, but the former would really be the true mainspring of the action.
But this very difference of universal consciousness and single self is what has sublated itself, and whose sublating is conscience.

The immediate knowing of the self that is certain of itself is law and duty; its intention is thereby, that it is its intention, the right; it is only required that it know this, and that it say this, namely that it has the conviction that its knowing and willing are the right.

The uttering of this assurance sublates, on its own account, the form of its particularity; in it, it acknowledges the necessary universality of the self; in calling itself conscience, it calls itself pure self-knowing and pure abstract willing, i.e. it calls itself a universal knowing and willing which acknowledges the others, is equal to them, for they are precisely this pure self-knowing and willing, and which is therefore also acknowledged by them.
In the willing of the self that is certain of itself, in this knowing that the self is the essence, lies the essence of the right.
– Whoever, then, says that he acts thus from conscience, speaks the truth, for his conscience is the self that knows and wills.
But he must essentially say this, for this self must at the same time be a universal self.

It is not this in the content of the action, for this content is on account of its determinacy in itself indifferent; rather, the universality lies in the form of the action; it is this form that is to be posited as actual; it is the self which as such is actual in language, declares itself as the true, and precisely therein acknowledges all selves and is acknowledged by them.
zh: 无论“出于对义务的信念而行动”这一保证是不是真的，无论所做之事确实是不是义务——这些问题或怀疑，对良心来说都没有意义。
——在“这一保证是否是真的”这个问题中，人们会预设：内在的意图不同于所标榜出来的意图，也就是说，单个自我的意愿能够把自己同义务、同普遍而纯粹的意识的意志分离开；后者被放进言谈之中，前者才实际上是行动真正的推动力。
然而，恰恰是这个普遍意识与单个自我的差别自己扬弃了自己，而对这个差别的扬弃就是良心。
那个对自己确有把握的自我的直接知识，就是法则和义务；它的意图正因为是它的意图，就是正当的东西；只要求它知道这一点，并说出这一点：即它确信，它的知识与意愿就是正当的东西。
把这种保证说出，本身就在扬弃它的特殊性的形式；它在其中承认自我的必然的普遍性；当它把自己称作良心时，它把自己称作纯粹的自身知识和纯粹的抽象意愿，也就是说，它把自己称作一种普遍的知识与意愿，这种知识与意愿承认他人、与他人相同，因为他们正是这种纯粹的自身知识与意愿，因此它也被他们承认。
在对自我确有把握的自我的意愿中，在“自我就是本质”这一知识中，存在着正当者的本质。
——所以，谁说自己出于良心而这样行动，谁说的就是真话，因为他的良心就是那知晓着、意愿着的自我。
但他必须本质上说出这一点，因为这个自我必须同时是普遍的自我。
它不是行动的内容中的普遍自我，因为内容就其规定性而言自在地无关紧要；相反，普遍性在于行动的形式；正是这种形式要被设定为现实的；它就是那个自我，这个自我作为这样的东西在语言中是现实的，把自己言说为真的东西，正因此承认一切自我、也被它们所承认。

en: Conscience, then, in the majesty of its exaltation above the determinate law and every content of duty, puts the arbitrary content into its knowing and willing; it is the moral genius which knows the inner voice of its immediate knowing as a divine voice, and since in this knowing it just as immediately knows determinate being, it is the divine creative power which has vitality in its concept.
It is likewise the divine worship within itself; for its acting is the intuiting of this its own divinity.
zh: 良心于是带着它凌驾于特定法则和一切义务内容之上的崇高威严，把任意的内容放进自己的知识与意愿之中；它是道德的天才，它把自己直接知识的内在声音知晓为神性的声音，而由于它在这种知识上同样直接地知晓着定在，它就是神性的创造力，这种创造力在自己的概念中具有生命力。
它同样是在自身之内的礼拜；因为它的行动就是对它自身这种神性的直观。

en: This solitary divine worship is at the same time essentially the divine worship of a community, and the pure inner knowing and hearing of oneself advances to the moment of consciousness.
The intuiting of itself is its objective determinate being, and this objective element is the uttering of its knowing and willing as a universal.
Through this uttering the self becomes something valid and the action becomes an executed deed.

The actuality and the subsistence of its doing is the universal self-consciousness; but the uttering of conscience posits the certainty of itself as a pure and thereby as a universal self; the others let the action count for the sake of this speech, in which the self is expressed and acknowledged as the essence.

The spirit and the substance of their association is thus the mutual assurance of their conscientiousness and good intentions, the delight in this reciprocal purity and the refreshment in the glory of the knowing and uttering, of cherishing and fostering such excellence.

– Insofar as this conscience still distinguishes its abstract consciousness from its self-consciousness, it has its life only hidden in God; he is indeed immediately present to its spirit and heart, to its self; but what is manifest, its actual consciousness and the mediating movement of the same, is for it an Other than that hidden interior and the immediacy of the present essence.
But in the consummation of conscience, the difference of its abstract consciousness and its self-consciousness sublates itself.

It knows that the abstract consciousness is precisely this self, this being-for-itself that is certain of itself, and that in the immediacy of the self's relation to the in-itself — which, posited outside the self, is the abstract essence and what is hidden from it — precisely this diversity is sublated.

For that relation is a mediating one, in which the related terms are not one and the same, but an Other for each other and are one only in a third; the immediate relation, however, in fact means nothing other than the unity.

Consciousness, raised above the thoughtlessness of still holding these differences, which are none, to be differences, knows the immediacy of the presence of the essence in it as the unity of the essence and its self, hence its self as the living in-itself, and this its knowing as the religion which, as intuited or existent knowing, is the speech of the community about its spirit.
zh: 这种孤独的礼拜本质上同时是一个教团的礼拜，而那种纯粹的、内在的、对自身的知晓与听闻进展到意识这一环节。
对它的直观就是它的对象性的定在，而这一对象性的要素，就是把它作为普遍者的知识与意愿说出来。
通过这种说出，自我成为有效的东西，行动成为执行出来的行动。
他的行动的现实性和持存，就是普遍的自我意识；而良心的说出则把自身的确定性设定为纯粹的、因而也是普遍的自我；他人正因为这种言谈——自我在其中被表达为、被承认为本质——而让行动有效。
因而，他们相互结合的意识和实体，就是相互保证各自的良心性和良好意图，是对这种相互的纯粹性的愉悦，是以知识、说出以及培育和照料这种卓越的荣耀为滋养。
——只要这个良心还把它抽象的意识同它的自我意识区分开来，它就只是把它的生命隐藏于上帝之中；上帝固然直接呈现在它的精神和心面前，呈现在它的自我面前；但那个公开的东西，即它的现实意识以及这种意识的中介着的运动，对它来说是不同于那隐藏的内在和当下本质的直接性的另一个东西。
然而在良心的完成中，它抽象的意识与它的自我意识之间的差别就自行扬弃了。
它知道，抽象的意识恰恰就是这个自我、这个对自己确有把握的自为存在，而且，在自我同自在的关系的直接性中——这个自在被设定于自我之外，是抽象的本质、是向它隐藏着的东西——恰恰是这种相异性被扬弃了。
因为那种关系是一种中介着的关系，在这种关系中，被关联的双方不是同一个东西，而是彼此互为另一个东西，并且只在第三者中才是统一的；而直接的关系实际上无非就叫统一。
意识上升到超出那种无思想性——即还把那些其实不是差别的差别当作差别——之后，知道本质在它之中的在场的直接性，就是本质与其自我的统一，因而知道它的自我就是有生命力的自在，知道它的这种知识就是宗教，这种宗教作为被直观着的知识或定在着的知识，是教团对其精神的言说。

en: We see herewith self-consciousness withdrawn into its innermost, for which all externality as such vanishes, — into the intuiting of Ich = Ich, in which this I is all essentiality and determinate being.

It sinks in this concept of itself, for it is driven to the extreme point of its extremes, and indeed in such a way that the distinct moments through which it is real or is still consciousness are not for us merely these pure extremes, but what it is for itself, what is in-itself for it and what is determinate being for it is volatilized into abstractions which have no support, no substance any more for this consciousness itself; and everything that was previously essence for the consciousness has withdrawn into these abstractions.

– Purified to this purity, consciousness is its poorest shape, and the poverty which constitutes its only possession is itself a vanishing; this absolute certainty into which the substance has dissolved is the absolute untruth that collapses into itself; it is the absolute self-consciousness in which consciousness sinks.
zh: 我们在这里看到自我意识退回到它的最内在之处，对于这个最内在之处，一切外在性作为外在性都消失了——退回到对 Ich = Ich 的直观，在这种直观中，这个我是一切本质性和定在。
它沉没在它自身的这个概念中，因为它被驱赶到它诸极端的尖端，而且是这样：那些使它成为实在的、或者说仍是意识的诸多有差别的环节，对我们来说不只是这些纯粹的极端，而且，它自为地所是的东西、对它在自在地所是的东西、对它是定在的东西，都挥发成了抽象物，这些抽象物对这个意识本身不再有任何支撑、任何实体；而一切此前对这个意识曾是本质的东西，都已回到这些抽象物之中。
——被纯化到这种纯粹性的意识，是它最贫乏的形态，而构成它唯一财富的那种贫乏，本身是一种消失；这种实体已消解于其中的绝对确定性，是自行坍缩的绝对非真理；它就是意识沉没于其中的绝对自我意识。

en: Considering this sinking within itself, then, for the consciousness the substance existing in itself is the knowing as its knowing.

As consciousness it is separated into the opposition of itself and the object, which is for it the essence; but this object is precisely the completely transparent; it is its self, and its consciousness is only the knowing of itself.
All life and all spiritual essentiality has withdrawn into this self and has lost its diversity from the I-self.
